title: Ang 83–91: Sri Rag ki Var
hookLine: Guru Ram Das's ballad with saloks
tomorrow: who gets the last word in the Granth's first raga?

lines: A BEAT FROM A PASSING CAR.
cards: Some songs land in your chest before you've caught a single word: a drumline, a crowd chanting a name, a bhangra beat rolling out of a passing car. You feel the rhythm first and the meaning second.
So why would a book of hymns hold a ballad? On ang 83 the Granth turns to its first var: a ballad, built to be sung, with a beat you could tap on your knee.

teach.b: Sri Rag ki Var is Guru Ram Das's ballad, and it moves in two voices. The pauris are its stanzas, his own, each one a step forward.
Before each pauri come saloks, short verses, some by other Gurus, set in front like a call before the answer. Short, then full. Salok, then pauri.
Once you hear the pattern, you can feel it coming. The very first salok, on ang 83, is by Guru Amar Das, and it's about music itself.

teach.h: SRI RAG IS BEST, IF IT CARRIES LOVE.
teach.b: In paraphrase: among the ragas, Sri Rag is the best, if through it you come to love the True One. Notice the if. The finest music counts when it carries love.
Without that, it's only a lovely sound.
And the hero of this ballad isn't a warrior riding into battle. The pauris praise the One, the Creator who made the world and watches over it.
So the Granth borrows the ballad's drive, the beat that makes you lean in, and points it somewhere new.
At the gurdwara, ragis sing it with harmonium and tabla, and the room feels the rhythm before it catches every word. That's the senses doing their job: the beat carries you to the meaning.

how: At the gurdwara, ragis sing the Granth's vars in kirtan with harmonium and tabla, singing a salok and then its pauri; Sikhs reading in order reach Sri Rag ki Var near the end of Sri Rag.

s: the first salok of Sri Rag ki Var calls Sri Rag the best of the ragas
with a condition: if through it you come to love the True One.
every line of a var is by the same Guru
the pauris are the var's author's; the saloks set before them include other Gurus' verses.
a var in the Granth is a battle song about a warrior
it keeps the ballad's drive, but the pauris praise the One.

games.q: you're choosing music for your grandparents' anniversary. your cousin says the most beautiful raga is enough on its own. what does the first salok of Sri Rag ki Var add?
o: only Sri Rag belongs at a Sikh family gathering.
the music doesn't matter at all; only the words count.
the finest music counts when it carries love for the True One.
games.why: Guru Amar Das calls Sri Rag the best of the ragas, then adds the if: if through it you come to love the True One.

practice: Find a salok near ang 84 in a Gurbani app, or use today's: among the ragas, Sri Rag is the best, if it carries love for the True One. Say it once in a low voice and tap the beat on your knee as you go.
Then stop tapping, and let whatever sound is in the room, a fan, traffic, your own breath, carry the rest of the sit.

carryVoice: Hum it on the way out: the first var, salok then pauri, call then answer. That one's sung.
